clue.text: Turk who served rum in jars, say

indicators.note: rum in its sense of odd or strange signals that the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Turkish waiter pours out rum stored in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being served, but it means odd and signals rearranging IN JARS SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Janissaries were the elite infantry soldiers who served the Ottoman sultans.

clue.text: Primate turned up to perform christening each year

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to christen a child is to name it
PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A priest arrives every year to carry out a baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NAMEPA, reading upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An apeman is a hypothetical primate between ape and human, or a person likened to an ape.

clue.text: Crowd suddenly arriving and occupying plant

parts.note: someone occupying a place is in it
a rush is a marsh plant

explanation.surface: A sudden mob turns up and takes over a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory being occupied, but it is the reed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden influx, such as a mass of people pouring in at once.

clue.text: Only fish left — chippy's closing

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: the closing letter of a word is its last one, so take the end of chippy

explanation.surface: The fish and chip shop is shutting, and it has only fish left.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for a fish and chip shop; its closing letter is Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Solely and only are synonyms, both meaning exclusively, with nothing else involved.

clue.text: Fix radius on out-and-out circular construction

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so radius comes before the shuffled letters
out, as in out of order or put out, signals that the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder sets a radius on a thoroughly circular structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-and-out' reads as one adjective but splits: the final 'out' shuffles OUT AND into OTUNDA, which follows R. 'Fix' just means set.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, typically topped with a dome.

clue.text: A doctor agitated over check for instrument

indicators.note: here over means covering, so the shuffled letters lie around the next piece
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A flustered physician hovers over a medical check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means around: the shuffled letters wrap the check piece. CH for check comes from chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: An octachord is an eight-stringed musical instrument, or a scale of eight notes.

clue.text: Proceeded cautiously about live broadcast turned into fiction

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to nose forward is to move ahead carefully, as a car into traffic

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of live are strewn about

explanation.surface: A cautious reporter edged around a live broadcast that became fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns LIVE into VELI, which NOSED goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To novelise a story, such as a film script, is to rewrite it as a novel.

clue.text: Break down style in art and poems, differently

parts.note: Deco, short for Art Deco, is a style in art and design

indicators.note: differently signals the letters of poems are put in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A critic analyses style in art and poetry from different angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' turns POEMS into MPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decompose is to rot or break down into constituent parts.

clue.text: Dramatic scenes, initially, having some impact on election

indicators.note: the words have some of the letters of the answer, so it is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Dramatic opening events sway the result of a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letters signal, but it belongs to the definition: the first scenes of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The first act of a play holds its opening scenes.

clue.text: Briefly mad about it in heated state

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
mad means crazed, so the letters of briefly are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone briefly loses their temper over something while fevered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns BRIEFLY into FEBRIL...Y, which goes 'about' IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrility is feverishness, the condition of a body running a high temperature.

clue.text: View outside broadcast, back in pavilion

parts.note: to gaze is to look at, or view

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for outside broadcast

explanation.surface: A TV crew watches an outside broadcast from back in the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OB into BO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion or summerhouse.

clue.text: Wet area damages bit of bridge across lake

parts.note: mars means spoils or damages

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the bridge piece reaches over the lake letter

parts.note: a hand is part of a game of the card game bridge
L is a standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Flooding from a lake damages part of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' is the card game, not a span over water; 'across' puts HAND around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshland is low, soggy ground that is often waterlogged.

clue.text: Tiny border in middle part of Irish plan

definitions.note: a noun here, a nickname for a small person

indicators.note: in places the border inside the selected letters
the middle part of the words Irish plan is their central letters

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A small boundary sits at the centre of an Irish plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle part of' takes SHP, the central three of IRISHPLAN; RIM goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is slang for a very small person, as is the nickname Tiny.

clue.text: Philosophical attitude shown as a monk is leading mass

indicators.note: leading means coming ahead, so the earlier pieces precede the mass letter

parts.note: a prior is a monk heading a priory
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A monk stands at the front of a church service, showing his philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like the church service but is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Apriorism is the philosophical stance of reasoning from principles prior to experience.

clue.text: Historic vessel is liable to sink with fellow aboard

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the fellow letter is put within the other pieces

parts.note: may expresses possibility, what is liable to happen
to sink is to lower

explanation.surface: An old ship could go down with one of the crew still on board.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620.

clue.text: Meeting places for judge and working groups set outside court

indicators.note: set outside means the unions piece is placed around the court letters

parts.note: trade unions are groups of workers

explanation.surface: A judge and trade unions meet outside the courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Junctions are points where roads or railways meet.

clue.text: Musical ability that's central throughout rehearsal clearly heard

indicators.note: the letters sitting at the very centre of rehearsal are taken

explanation.surface: A good ear is needed throughout rehearsal, so music is clearly heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The same three letters are also central in 'heard', which 'clearly heard' points to as a second instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an ear for music means a natural talent for pitch and melody.

clue.text: Period starts or ends in Europe, remember — also Asia or Africa

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of the words that follow are taken

parts.note: the run of letters across remember also that spells the answer is a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: A history lesson on an age that began or ended in Europe, Asia or Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends work too: europE, rememberR, asiA or africA; and 'also' or 'Africa' could replace Asia among the starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long historical age or epoch.

clue.text: Whiskey or port

definitions.meaning: ... is a whiskey distilled from ... grain
A historic port town in East Sussex, England

explanation.definitionFit: Rye names both a grain-based whiskey and an old Sussex port town.

clue.text: Annoying person necessitating change of earplug

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are put in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone so irritating you need to swap your earplugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaguer is someone who pesters or torments others.

clue.text: Awfully sorry about return of weekend letters? Special deliveries

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next piece
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of sorry are scrambled
return means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the letters at the end of week are E and K

explanation.surface: A postman apologises for the late return of weekend mail sent special delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' makes YOR..RS from SORRY; 'return of' turns EK, the end of 'week', to KE. A yorker is a cricket ball bowled to land at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkers are a special kind of ball, or delivery, bowled in cricket.

clue.text: Vote for one of two in fairly violent exchange, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is spoken, a soundalike

parts.words: one of two in fairly violent exchange
parts.note: an eye for an eye is a fair, if violent, exchange with two eyes in it

explanation.surface: Voting yes is one side of a fairly heated argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The exchange is 'an eye for an eye', a just but violent retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is the parliamentary word for a vote in favour.

clue.text: Raised purchase price, ultimately screening available website

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the outer pieces enclose the next
in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
a book that is out is published and available

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of price

explanation.surface: A raised purchase price eventually shows up on what is available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns BUY to YUB; with E it is 'screening' OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: YouTube is the online video-sharing site.

clue.text: Held by fine performance as it happens

parts.note: something held by a person is in their hands
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an act is a stage performance

explanation.surface: A fine show is put on, as it turns out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for actually, used like as it happens to introduce a surprising truth.

clue.text: Key man on board is run into a lot

parts.note: the king, key piece on a chessboard, is K in chess notation
to meet someone is to run into them

explanation.surface: An important man on the company board stumbles into a great deal of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot in the sense of one's fate or destiny is a synonym of kismet.

clue.text: Release granny, say, from trunk? No thanks!

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An offer to free Grandma from a car boot is declined.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny is a type of knot, so releasing it is untying it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknot a granny knot is to untie it.

clue.text: Very bad part — character in Romeo and Juliet

parts.note: to part is to separate, or sever
the only letter both names contain is E

explanation.surface: A dreadful part for an actor in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, not a role: E is the one letter in both ROMEO and JULIET.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe injury or storm is a very bad one.

clue.text: Cuts food in way that's right in summer months

indicators.note: in places the right inside the summer months

parts.note: Junes are summer months in the northern hemisphere
a lien is a legal right over another's property

explanation.surface: Someone slices food in a style that suits the summer months.
explanation.definitionFit: To julienne is to cut vegetables into thin matchstick strips.

clue.text: Raw recruit that is seen by castle

parts.note: the rook is also called the castle in chess
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A new soldier is seen standing next to a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer, especially a raw army recruit, in informal usage.

clue.text: Get me and you, finally, organised more than before

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of you

explanation.surface: Our group has grown now that you and I are organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges GETMEAND plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something augmented has been increased, so it is more than before.

clue.text: Getting, since believing?

definitions.meaning: getting a joke is ... it, understanding
... that means since, as a conjunction
the proverb ... is believing equates the two

explanation.definitionFit: Seeing means understanding, given that, and, by the proverb, believing.

clue.text: Seating put back around piano — time for some music

indicators.note: around means the reversed seating goes about the next pieces
put back means reversed, the letters read from the end

parts.note: settees are sofas, a form of seating
P is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: Chairs are returned around the piano in time for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns SETTEES into SEETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Septettes are compositions for seven performers.
